Both record_undo/3 and record_batch_undo/2 in Barkpark.Plugins.Sheets.Session.Ops are PUBLIC functions operating on a plain map (`%{undo: %{}, redo: %{}}` is sufficient shape -- push_stack/put_stack only do Map.fetch!(state, key)). recipes.claim: record_undo/3 and record_batch_undo/2 are public (def) functions in Session.Ops that only need a plain map with :undo/:redo keys -- push_stack/put_stack call Map.fetch!(state, key), no struct, no DB field required
@undo_depth is 100, defined once at the top of ops.ex, and is the ONLY bound applied by push_stack -- it bounds per-key list length via Enum.take, never the number of distinct keys in the outer map

500 distinct client-supplied 'user' strings produce map_size(state.undo) == 500 (unbounded key growth), computed via a PURE function call with `mix run --no-start` -- zero app boot, zero DB, zero GenServer/Session/DynamicSupervisor in the call path
recipes.rerun: cd /Volumes/SATECHI/github/barkpark/api && mix run --no-start -e 'alias Barkpark.Plugins.Sheets.Session.Ops; state = Enum.reduce(1..500, %{undo: %{}, redo: %{}}, fn i, s -> Ops.record_undo(s, %{"op" => "set_cell", "user" => "user-#{i}"}, %{"op" => "clear_cell", "user" => "user-#{i}"}) end); IO.puts(map_size(state.undo))'

recipes.claim: the SAME pure call, repeated 500x for ONE user instead of 500 distinct users, caps the per-key stack at exactly 100 (proves depth-is-capped-per-key is real and NOT what is broken -- the outer key-count is the unbounded axis)
